title: LoopSettle: an open simulator of circular liquidity in instant payment systems
description: LoopSettle measures how much of the liquidity an instant payment system (such as Brazil's Pix) requires corresponds to circular flow, how much of it can actually be recovered under real settlement rules, and at what cost in delay. It generates synthetic payment flows calibrated to public aggregates, settles them under several designs (real-time gross settlement, deferred netting, atomic micro-cycles, queues, gridlock resolution) and computes the liquidity floor: the least liquidity any mechanism that settles each payment within a deadline can need. It also runs on a user's own payment file, without the data leaving the machine. Written in Rust with no heavy dependencies; reproducible bit for bit across platforms; runs in a browser.
